title: SELinux Labels, Denials, and Least-privilege Policy Check

questions.prompt: Which approach best applies selinux labels, denials, and least-privilege policy?
options: Start from intended ownership and labels, then grant only the minimum access supported by threat model and negative tests.
questions.answer: Start from intended ownership and labels, then grant only the minimum access supported by threat model and negative tests.
questions.explanation: The correct response preserves authority, compatibility, exact artifact evidence, adverse-path behavior, and operational ownership.

questions.prompt: If a process has Linux root privileges, SELinux allow rules no longer constrain it.
questions.explanation: Generating and accepting every audit2allow suggestion converts observed behavior into broad authority without checking labels or architecture.

questions.prompt: What four elements identify a basic SELinux access decision?
questions.answer: Source type, target type, object class, and requested permission.
questions.explanation: The answer identifies the contract or mechanism that remains valid beyond one implementation demonstration.
